title: introduce-quantile-stabilizer-and-stochastic-prefetch-failure-injector
author: Anya Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed that small-scale noise in host allocator activity and intermittent prefetch failures create long-tail p95/p99 variance in several kernel profiles. Existing synthetic runners (burst, primer, sequenced replayers) exercise baseline load but do not exercise transient prefetch failure modes or quantify how quantile smoothing policies affect stability. This PR introduces two complementary components: (1) aQuantileStabilizer reporter that post-processes streaming latency histograms to compute stabilized quantile estimates across sliding epochs and (2) a StochasticPrefetchFailureInjector runner that injects controlled prefetch miss/latency events into the workload driver to emulate transient device/pagefault prefetech misses seen in certain GPU + nvme setups. Changes are intentionally modular and toggleable via runner flags and reporter config so we can A/B on canary clusters before wider adoption.

What this PR does (high level):
- New reporter: bench/reporters/quantile_stabilizer.py. Computes windowed quantile smoothing, exposes metrics: bench.quantile.stabilized.{p50,p90,p95,p99} and bench.quantile.raw.{p50,p90,p95,p99}. Supports exponential smoothing and epoch-based medians with configurable window_size and alpha.
- New runner: bench/runners/prefetch_injector.py. Extends the generic SequenceRunner with three failure modes: drop-prefetch, inject-latency, and delayed-kv-checkpoint. Each mode is parametrized (probability, latency_ms distribution, burst_length). Deterministic seed support added for reproducible experiments.
- Integration tests and e2e: tests/integration/test_prefetch_injector.py and tests/reporters/test_quantile_stabilizer.py. Tests cover determinism, metric naming, and basic stability under synthetic sequences.
- CI: Add bench pipeline job: .github/workflows/bench-stability.yml to run the new e2e tests and a lightweight simulated run in CI.
- Docs: docs/bench/quantile-stabilizer.md with usage examples and recommended config for canary runs.

Design notes:
- The QuantileStabilizer is intentionally conservative: by default it publishes raw quantiles and stabilized quantiles to allow side-by-side comparisons. We avoided overriding upstream histogram libraries; instead the reporter subscribes to histogram streams and computes stabilized values in a separate path (no change to source histograms).
- The PrefetchFailureInjector hooks into the existing SequenceRunner sampler so it reproduces realistic token timing and batching behavior; failure events are injected at sampling time rather than transport layer to keep the experiment focused on kernel-level prefetch impacts.

Compatibility and rollout plan:
- Feature flags: bench.enabled.reporters.quantile_stabilizer and bench.runners.prefetch_injector.enabled default to false in production config.
- Canaries: plan to run on perf-canary cluster (small GPU fleet) for 72h with controlled traffic patterns (see ENG-1987).

Test plan:
- Unit tests added for core math (alpha smoothing convergence, window eviction).
- Integration test uses deterministic RNG seed to assert reproducible metric traces across runs (seed included in CI).
- Small-scale perf run on perf-canary to validate no >1% steady-state throughput regression and to capture p99 delta under injected failures.

Backward compatibility: non-breaking. All changes are opt-in.

Notes for reviewers:
- The quantile reporter has a configurable memory ceiling (default 16MB) to avoid unbounded state; please double-check the eviction logic.
- I included a simple visual debugging CLI under bench/tools/plot_stabilizer.py — it's handy for local inspection but can be removed if preferred.

Related: ENG-1987 (p99 variance investigation), SUP-631 (customer report of intermittent tail spikes).

review_conversation:
Marcus Liu: Can we make the default window_size small (e.g. 5 epochs) in CI to speed tests?
Anya Patel: Done, CI uses window_size=5 via env override; production default stays 20.
Diego Fernández: Why inject at sampler level instead of transport? Won't that miss network-layer-induced prefetech failures?
Anya Patel: Transport-layer faults are orthogonal; we want to simulate device/prefetch-level misses that affect kernel scheduling and KV cache warmups. Injecting at sampler keeps the scope focused and reproduces token timing. We can add a transport-mode in a follow-up if needed.
Riley Thompson: Unit test for eviction looks racy in CI occasionally.
Anya Patel: Increased eviction test timeout and added deterministic seed; reran, passing.
Marcus Liu: Approve after addressing minor comment about metric naming (switch RAW -> raw).
Anya Patel: Renamed metrics and updated docs.
CI: bench-stability (matrix) -> pass.
Merge: squashed and merged via squash/merge by Anya Patel.
release_notes: Introduce a QuantileStabilizer reporter and a StochasticPrefetchFailureInjector runner to exercise transient prefetch failure modes and compute stabilized quantiles for more robust p95/p99 tracking. Opt-in via bench feature flags. Recommended for canary runs when investigating tail variance.
